notes:
Answered strictly from documented biography (Wikipedia; Britannica; Muhammad Ali Center official timeline; Jonathan Eig, 'Ali: A Life' (2017) and Thomas Hauser's oral biography as reported in secondary coverage; contemporaneous news reporting from NBC/CBS/BBC/Time/SI; Clay v. United States, 403 U.S. 698 (1971)). Part D omitted - this exercise forbade opening any reading, so no valid answer exists for D1-D8; no astrology source of any kind was consulted.

Core facts used: b. 17 Jan 1942, Louisville General Hospital, Louisville KY; d. 3 Jun 2016, Scottsdale AZ, aged 74, septic shock following a respiratory illness, with advanced Parkinson's syndrome (diagnosed Sept 1984 at Columbia Presbyterian; his physician Dr Dennis Cope attributed it to pugilistic brain syndrome, while Lonnie Ali reported doctors calling it non-boxing-related).

Item-by-item reasoning on the debatable answers:
A1/A2/A3 - the hospital birth is documented (Louisville General); NO clock time is reported in any biographical source I consulted, and I deliberately did not consult birth-data/astrology databases, so A2 is a genuine 'unknown'. A3 'no' means no rectification is documented in biography, not that none exists somewhere.
A4 'four_plus' - documented admissions include the Nov 1964 strangulated-hernia emergency (Wikipedia, Ali-Liston II), the Mar 1973 broken jaw (Norton I), the 1980 Mayo Clinic workup, Sept 1984 Columbia Presbyterian, Dec 2014 (UTI, initially reported as pneumonia), Jan 2015, and Jun 2016.
A5 'two_plus' - hernia surgery 13 Nov 1964 (three days before the scheduled Liston rematch, which it postponed) plus spinal-stenosis surgery in the early 2010s; the 1973 jaw was also surgically wired.
A6 - recurring: brain/head (Parkinson's syndrome, the Mayo report of a hole in the brain's outer layer), voice/throat (his slurring was the signature symptom), nerves (the disease is neurological, with tremor), back/spine (spinal stenosis), urinary (recurrent UTIs 2014-15), chest/lungs (repeated respiratory infections/pneumonia in his last years). Jaw is excluded as a single injury, not recurring.
A7 'robust' - an inference, flagged as such: no childhood illness appears anywhere in a very heavily documented childhood, and family accounts stress extraordinary physical energy. A8 is left 'unknown' because no near-death childhood event is documented at all.
A9 '70_80' - from genealogy records: Herman Heaton Clay 1876-1954 (77), Edith Greathouse Clay 1890-1971 (81), John Lewis Grady 1886-1965 (79), Birdie Morehead 1894-1944 (50); mean 71.75. Genealogy-site sourcing, so moderate confidence.
A10 'conflicted' - Cassius Clay Sr. (1912-1990) was a heavy drinker with a record for reckless driving, disorderly conduct and assault and battery, publicly denounced his son's Nation of Islam affiliation, and Ali was explicit that he was far closer to his mother ('Bird': 'there's no one who's been better to me my whole life'). A11 'steady' - Sr. worked continuously as a sign and billboard painter; no documented reversal.
A14 'higher_secondary' - graduated Central High School, Louisville, 1960, ranked 376th of 391; dyslexic. A15 'no' - his schooling was impaired but not interrupted. C4 (higher study) is scored as difficulty at confidence 5: no tertiary education at all, plus the failed Army qualifying test.
A16/A17/A18 - the option list has no 'sport/athletics' entry, which is the single biggest fit problem in this questionnaire for Ali. He was a self-employed professional prizefighter (professional_practice) who also ran businesses (Champburger, Muhammad Ali Enterprises). A18 selections are the genuine non-boxing ones: performance (Broadway 'Buck White', films, Grammy-nominated spoken-word records), writing/media (poetry, two autobiographies, lifelong media presence) and religious/charitable work (Nation of Islam ministry, UN Messenger of Peace 1998, hostage negotiation in Iraq 1990). No athletic option existed to select.
A21 'net_loss' - as an observant Muslim he did not gamble; this answer reflects documented investment/business losses ('large sums seemingly disappeared into poor business investments'), which is the only sense in which the item applies. A22 'none' - no inheritance or windfall is documented; the 2006 sale of 80% of his name-and-likeness rights was a sale of an earned asset, not a windfall.
A23 'serious_past' - weakest-sourced answer here. Documented: no income and heavy legal costs across the 1967-1970 exile, survival on college speaking fees, and repeated reporting of debt from lavish spending and bad investments; his estate was nevertheless valued at roughly $50-80m. Financial-press sourcing rather than a biography, so treat as moderate confidence.
A24-A27 - four marriages: Sonji Roi (m. 14 Aug 1964, div. 1966), Belinda Boyd/Khalilah (m. 17 Aug 1967, div. 1976-77), Veronica Porche (m. 1977, div. 1986), Lonnie Williams (m. 19 Nov 1986, until his death). He died married, so A24 'married'. A27 'mixed' rather than 'happy' or 'ended': the final marriage was stable to the end, but three preceding marriages ended in divorce with well-documented infidelity. A25 gives the FIRST marriage year (1964), matching the template's convention. A26 'on_time' - married at 22, unremarkable against his family's pattern.
A28 'three_plus' - nine acknowledged children: Maryum (1968), twins Jamillah and Rasheda (1970), Muhammad Ali Jr. (1972), Miya (1972), Khaliah (1974), Hana (1976), Laila (30 Dec 1977), and Asaad (adopted 1986). A29 'no' - no fertility difficulty or child loss documented.
A30 - Eig's research describes him as gregarious, charming, funny, boastful, trusting and generous, 'excessively arrogant' and equally naive, 'the spirit of a rebel'. 'practical' is deliberately NOT selected: his financial impracticality is one of the best-documented things about him. 'quick_tempered' is NOT selected: aggression was ring-bound, not temperamental.
A31 'no' - the 1967-1970 exile was plainly a period of severe strain (title stripped, passport confiscated, death threats, FBI surveillance) but no diagnosis or treatment for depression or anxiety is documented; commentators describe his coping as 'adaptive and impressively functional'.
A33 'over5' - he left Louisville at 18 and lived in Miami, Chicago, Cherry Hill NJ, Deer Lake PA, Los Angeles, Berrien Springs MI and Scottsdale AZ; 'abroad' is not selected because his long foreign stays (Zaire, Manila) were training camps, not residence. A34 'brief' - eight to ten days in Dade County Jail from 16 Dec 1968 on an old driving-without-a-licence conviction; he never served the draft-evasion sentence, being free on appeal until the 8-0 reversal.
A35 - twelve dated turning points, weighted toward career/legal because B6 already carries the family ones: Oct 1954 stolen bicycle and first meeting with Joe Martin (coded 'other' - the start of boxing but not yet a job); Sept 1960 Olympic gold in Rome; Oct 1960 professional contract with the Louisville Sponsoring Group; Feb 1964 title win over Liston; Feb 1964 announcement of conversion to Islam and the name change; Aug 1964 first marriage; Apr 1967 refusal of induction (title stripped, licence revoked, convicted that June); Jun 1971 Supreme Court reversal; Oct 1974 Rumble in the Jungle; Dec 1981 final fight (Berbick) and retirement, coded job_loss as the nearest available code for the end of a vocation; Sept 1984 Parkinson's diagnosis; Jul 1996 lighting the Olympic cauldron in Atlanta. Not enough rows for: Aug 1967 second marriage, Oct 1970 comeback v Quarry, Mar 1971 and Oct 1975 Frazier fights, Mar 1973 broken jaw, 1977 third marriage, Nov 1986 fourth marriage, Nov 1990 Iraq hostage release, Sept 1998 UN Messenger of Peace, Nov 2005 Presidential Medal of Freedom and the opening of the Ali Center.
A36 'same' - he died in 2016, so there is no post-2023 period to compare; 'same' is the only non-fabricating answer.
B1 'opt1' - the self-proclaimed Greatest, 'wants to be seen and respected, generous, proud, does not take correction easily', is an almost verbatim description of the documented Ali. B2 'lean_tall' - 6ft 3in, fighting at 210-236 lb; his weight did fluctuate badly between camps late in his career, which is the argument for 'solid_heavy', but lean-and-tall fits the documented physique better. B3 'younger' - he was noted throughout his career for an unmarked, youthful face and traded on it verbally. B4 'eldest' - older of two; Rahaman (1943-2025) survived him. B5 'hospital'.
B6 - father d. 8 Feb 1990; mother d. 20 Aug 1994 (heart failure, aged 77); first marriage Aug 1964; first job Oct 1960 (pro contract; the amateur career from 1954 is not a job); own surgery Nov 1964 (strangulated hernia); first child Maryum in 1968 (month omitted - I could not confirm the exact date from a source I trust).
Part C reasoning: C1 difficulty at 5 (32 years of Parkinson's). C2 'gone well' at 4 - the 6th-house sense of enemies/opposition went unusually well for him: 56-5 in the ring and an 8-0 Supreme Court reversal of the government's case against him. C3 difficulty at 4 - the most articulate athlete in history lost his voice to the disease; his slurred speech was the first and most public symptom. C5 'gone well' at 4 - global fortune, foreign travel and fame far beyond his origins. C6 'gone well' at 3 - substantial property and assets, tempered by heavy losses. C7 'gone well' at 4 - roughly $60m in career earnings in 1960s-70s dollars; the highest-paid athlete of his era. C8 difficulty at 3 - repeatedly exploited by managers, advisers and business partners (Eig: naive and generous, 'exploited over and over again'), plus three failed marriages; the Louisville Sponsoring Group, Angelo Dundee and Bundini Brown are the counter-evidence, hence only confidence 3. C9 'gone well' at 5 - Sportsman of the Century, BBC Sports Personality of the Century, Presidential Medal of Freedom, UN Messenger of Peace, despite the 1967-70 vilification. C10 difficulty at 4 - three divorces and documented infidelity. C11 'genuinely both' at 4 - faith was central and sustaining, and it also cost him his title, his prime years and, in the Nation of Islam period, his relationship with Malcolm X, which he later called a regret. C12 difficulty at 3 - no gambling, and his unearned/passive money (investments, business ventures) consistently lost.
